title: Merged review result (review-result.json)
$comment: `additionalProperties: false` marks the known key set, but validate.py enforces it SOFTLY: unknown keys are stripped with a logged warning before the strict pass, rather than failing the gate closed. A review that ran must never have its findings discarded over a cosmetic extra key — the merge copies specialist findings forward, so a key borrowed from another finding vocabulary arrives here too. Value validation of the known keys stays strict, so everything the verdict and the disposition check read still fails closed.

comment_body.description: The review comment's markdown, or null when the run produced no prose. render_comment.py already treats a non-string body as blank and falls back to a machine-rendered body plus a `::warning::` — a designed degradation. Failing the gate closed on the null instead would block the PR outright and post nothing, which is strictly worse than the fallback the renderer was built for. `findings` and `disposition` are NOT nullable by contrast: the validator iterates both, and a null there is a broken run with no safe reading.

file.description: File anchor, or null when the finding has none. The key stays required — the model must state the anchor — but its value may be null, for the same reason `line` may: repo-wide, convention, and architectural findings are properties of the tree rather than of one file, and a schema that rejects the null a model naturally writes would fail the gate closed on exactly the findings that most need a human.

line.description: Line anchor, or null when the finding has none. Null is accepted as well as omission: repo-wide, convention, and architectural findings have no single line, and a schema that rejects the null a model naturally writes would fail the gate closed on exactly the findings that most need a human.

body.description: Elaboration, or null when the finding needs none. The field is optional, so absence is already legal; null is that same absence spelled the way a model writes it, and no consumer reads it as anything but text-or-nothing.

confidence.description: Self-reported confidence in 0..1, or null when the specialist has none to offer. Optional like `body`, nullable for the same reason; no script reads it, so a null costs nothing and a rejected null costs the whole run. The bounds still apply to any number given.

note.description: Why the finding was handled this way. Optional for `kept`/`merged`, where null is just the model's spelling of the absence the schema already allows. A `downgraded` or `dropped` entry still needs a real reason: the conditional below demands a string there, so widening this type does not let a null satisfy the one place a note is load-bearing.
